:::{#about}

I build the tools, reports and analysis pipelines that turn environmental monitoring data into decisions.

I'm a senior consultant at WSP (formerly Ricardo), where I write reproducible reports for UK government clients, build Shiny apps and internal R packages, and train analysts. Outside of client work I'm a core maintainer of the [openair](https://openair-project.github.io/openair/) family of open-source R packages, used by air quality professionals around the world.

Before consultancy I did a PhD in atmospheric chemistry at the University of York, using statistical modelling on hundreds of thousands of on-road vehicle measurements to calculate emission factors.

:::

## What I do

- **R package development.** I maintain {openair}, {openairmaps}, {worldmet} and {deweather}. I also wrote {ukaq}, {euroaq} and {leaf.magic}, and I've had features merged into open source projects like {leaflet}, {dygraphs} and {prismatic}.

- **Reproducible reporting.** Quarto reports that go from raw monitoring data to published output, including annual network reports for Defra.

- **Data visualisation.** Static and interactive graphics with ggplot2, plotnine, leaflet, gt and Observable. Runner-up and honourable mention in the Posit Table Contest.

- **Shiny apps.** Dashboards and internal tools for clients and colleagues.

- **Teaching.** Posit Certified Tidyverse Instructor. I've taught R to analysts from Defra, the Environment Agency, UKHSA, UKCEH and CASANZ.
